proposal:
VERDICT: no credible universal mechanism and no polynomial SAT algorithm. Everything below is hand-derived, unexecuted and not machine-checked. One EXPERIMENT outside scc-emra-ialh5-v1: PCA, partition-cell abstraction. It changes P7 (nonlinear gadgets untouched) and gives a non-linear answer to U8 (fragility). I withdraw last round's remark that AND gadgets cannot compress: a quotient needs a surjection onto classes, not a bijective recoding.

REPRESENTATION. Z_S is the set of forbidden tuples on exact support S. Modules: v~w iff v and w occur in the same supports, so every support is a disjoint union of modules T_1..T_r. A partition system Pi splits each {0,1}^T into cells: explicit lists of projected tuples plus one implicit rest cell. The quotient Q_Pi has one multi-valued variable per module. It forbids a cell tuple in S iff the whole box c_1 x ... x c_r lies in Z_S, tested by |Z_S intersect box| = prod |c_i| (k-bit integers). Cells are coded in ceil(log2 c_T) bits, with unused codes forbidden.

HAND LEMMAS.
S7 (any Pi): Q_Pi composed with the cell map forbids a subset of what F forbids, so Q_Pi UNSAT implies F UNSAT. Certificate: cell lists plus one count equality per quotient clause, recheckable in O(Lk).
E1 (Nerode Pi: a~a' iff the slices Z_S[a] and Z_S[a'] agree for every S containing T): F = Q composed with pi, and pi is onto, so SAT transfers both ways.
N1: let F = G(g_1..g_n) with disjoint scopes, arbitrary Boolean gadgets, full fibre-product encoding and G twin-free. Then modules are the scopes, c_T <= 2, and Q is G minus irrelevant variables. This covers XOR, AND, MAJ and indexing.
N2: admissible groupings are exactly the refinements of the module partition, and c of a union is at most the product, so modules minimise the quotient bit count.

DISCOVERY (L = total literals, k = max width, m = clauses).
D0. Modules by partition refinement, O(L). SKIP RULE: if all modules are singletons, stop. This is the cost-aware exit for unstructured inputs.
D1. Profiles P(a) = set of (S, rest), one entry per tuple per module; sort.
Phase A. Link a,a' iff |P(a) intersect P(a')| > tau*max(|P(a)|,|P(a')|), with tau = 2/3. Cells are the components. Pairs come from an inverted index.
Phase B. Build Q_Pi and merge cells with identical quotient profiles. This is exact Nerode on Q, so no strength is lost. Repeat to fixpoint, at most L rounds.
Total: O(k^2 * sum|Z_S|^2 + L^2 k log L) bit operations. Q has at most m + sum c_T clauses, at most n bits and no wider blocks. The unchanged solver then runs on Q. UNSAT gives UNSAT. SAT with an exact Pi lifts through any cell representatives. SAT with a lossy Pi gives UNKNOWN and fallback.

R2 (hand). Let F = F0 plus extras E with the same modules, p(a) the base profile size and e(a) the number of extras projecting to a. If every cross-class pair has |P0(a) intersect P0(a')| + e(a) + e(a') <= tau*max(p(a),p(a')), then cells refine F0's classes and Q0 UNSAT implies Q_Pi UNSAT. Same-class pairs merge in phase A when max e < p(1/tau - 1). Otherwise phase B re-merges them unless a surviving extra box pins them.

REFUTED: tau = 1/2 (POM's threshold). In the 36-clause control take a module with polarities 2:1, a=00, a'=01 and extras (01,r1), (01,r2), (00,r3). The profiles have sizes 5 and 4 with overlap 3 > 2.5, so the classes merge wrongly and core clauses are lost. At tau = 2/3 the overlap is at most 3 against a maximum profile of at least 5 (36-clause) or 6 (96-clause). So no placement of one extra per block links across classes.

PREDICTIONS for the independent harness, not the deployed solver (fixture is null).
P8. auto00006 gives 6 modules of size 2 and 9 binary clauses on 6 bits. auto00007 gives 4 modules of size 3 and 6 binary clauses on 4 bits. Both match BLQ up to renaming.
P9. On both fragility fixtures Q is UNSAT. Bits are 6 (resp. 4) unless some extra tuple has both projections in phase-A singleton cells. Each such pin costs its two modules one extra cell.
P10. The K3,3 2-CNF lifted by AND, and the K4 2-CNF lifted by MAJ3 (96 width-6 clauses), give the same 9 and 6 binary clauses. BLQ's translation stabiliser is 0 on both.
missing_theorem:
M0: S7, E1, N1, N2, R2 and P8-P10 are hand arguments only.

FIRST UNSUPPORTED THEOREM, U13 (gadget coverage): every UNSAT lift G(g(x)) whose G the deployed solver rejects without branching is caught by PCA plus POM.

REFUTED BY HAND. A_ov: the K4 2-CNF with y_i = MAJ3 on overlapping scopes {1,2,3}, {3,4,5}, {5,6,7}, {7,8,1}. F is UNSAT because any composition with an UNSAT G is. All eight variables have distinct support-incidence sets (variable 2 lies in three supports, variable 1 in five), so all modules are singletons and PCA skips. MAJ3 fibres are not affine cosets, so POM cannot merge a whole fibre. Whether A_ov is hard for the deployed solver is untested.

REPAIRED CLAIM, U14 (unsupported, falsifiable). Take candidate scopes from pairwise support intersections. Test Z_S = proj_T(Z_S) join proj_T'(Z_S) for T union T' = S. Introduce one indicator per (scope, relation) and add binary clauses for disjoint, covering and nested relations on one scope. Every model of F induces indicator values satisfying all these clauses, so this is a sound UNSAT prefilter. On A_ov the intersections include the four scopes, each block is an exact join of two fibres, and the abstraction is G. It is not complete: with dependent forms a+b, b+c, a+c the abstraction can be SAT while F is UNSAT, and I know no polynomial exact treatment of such cross-scope dependencies.

STILL MISSING: any residual-state bound. An exact quotient Q can be an arbitrary hard CNF, so PCA shrinks search only on module-structured inputs.
self_attack:
1. Known mathematics. Exact cells are Freuder-style neighbourhood interchangeability on module meta-variables, and the lossy version is a domain-partition abstraction. The new content is only the module grouping with N2, width-free discovery, the A/B fixpoint, R2 and the tau refutation.
2. Module fragility. One clause on a new support cutting across two scopes splits the modules, and the skip rule then fires. Ignoring supports with a single tuple is an arms race, not a theorem.
3. tau is tuned to the receipts. p/2 extras on one value, or planted decoy boxes, break R2. A lossy Pi then yields a SAT quotient and UNKNOWN, which is pure overhead.
4. For c_T > 2 the bit code of the cells is arbitrary, and a bad code can make Q harder for the deployed solver than F. There is no peak(Q) <= peak(F) theorem, since the solver is not restriction-monotone (compare U10).
5. Dependent linear forms: the block on {a,b,c} forbidding 000 and 111 has only singleton cells, while POM merges it. PCA and POM are incomparable, and I have no unified object or composition order.
6. Cost. Phase A is quadratic in block size, on top of the measured ~22x IALH overhead on auto00006.
7. Deletions. Removing one tuple from a base box destroys that quotient clause, and no sound repair exists.
8. P9's bit count depends on where the extras sit, which I have not seen. Only the UNSAT part is placement-independent by my hand count.
mechanism_signature: PCA: support-twin module grouping plus cell partitions of module assignments. The quotient forbids only fully forbidden cell boxes, so it is sound for every partition and exact for the Nerode partition. Discovery is profile linking at tau=2/3 followed by an exact re-coarsening fixpoint, with a count-equality certificate and an O(L) skip when modules are singletons. Width-free and gadget-agnostic (non-affine), disjoint scopes only. Experiment outside scc-emra-ialh5-v1.
delta_from_prior:
POM merged affine cosets inside blocks and was a prefilter only.
New this round:
(1) Non-affine compression: classes come from profile equality with no linear algebra, so AND/MAJ lifts compress where BLQ gives W=0. Last round's AND remark is withdrawn.
(2) E1: a surjective quotient with two-way SAT transfer when the partition is exact.
(3) S7 holds for every partition, and degradation is graceful: a pinned module costs one cell instead of total collapse to 12 variables.
(4) POM's 1/2 threshold is refuted by an explicit placement in the 36-clause control; 2/3 survives by hand count.
(5) An O(L) skip criterion.
(6) Coverage claim U13 is refuted by the overlapping-MAJ3 adversary A_ov; U14 is stated as the next falsifiable claim.
(7) N2: module grouping is bit-optimal among exact groupings.
Unchanged: no residual-state bound and no universality claim.
